correctness.rationale: For a transitive conversely well-founded Kripke frame, depth-one types are (v,T) with v in finite V, T subset of successor valuations. Necessity of the least support closure follows by choosing a minimum ordinal rank occurrence of each type in the successor spectrum, using strictly rank-decreasing successors and transitivity U⊆T. Sufficiency constructs one representative per type, connects each supported T requirement to a type at a strictly earlier closure stage, takes transitive closure, and adjoins a root; each representative then has exactly its required successor-valuation set. This proves an iff for any finite valuation alphabet without relying on enumeration. With |V|=2, the eight possible depth-one types produce 256 spectra; independent separate bitmask fixed-point enumeration returned 85 realizable, with size histogram 1,2,5,12,21,22,15,6,1. Each possible root valuation doubles to 170 pointed depth-two types; finite characteristic formulas separate them, so all 2^170 subsets are definable even in the language permitting countable conjunctions. The given verify_depth2.py exhausts all 256, cross-checks permutations and constructs finite witnesses; finite check is exhaustive for the count while the structural theorem is independently proved.
